gap: No result ChatGPT got states an independent measured laser or print figure for any candidate. For example, 3DPrinting.com's Phillip Keane cut 8 mm wood in a single pass with the Snapmaker Artisan's 40 W laser, and 3D Printing Industry found its 40 W laser cut 5.2 mm basswood best at 1,300 mm/min and 90% power.
standout_why: I compared against four pages. desktop3dprinters.us/topics/3d-printer-laser-combos (cited) and desktop3dprinters.us/lists/3d-printers-with-laser-engraver give only the makers' spec-sheet figures (10 W cuts 5 mm, 40 W cuts 15 mm basswood plywood) and say outright that they have no measured values. 3dengr.com (cited) gives no figures at all; it says only that 'reviewers generally describe' the laser. Tom's Hardware's best-3D-printers page (cited) and its H2D review returned only the page title to my fetches, so I could not check them for numbers. None of the pages I could read has a reviewer-measured cut, a speed and power setting, a print time or an accuracy figure.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. The independent tests show the 15 mm cut figure that rivals and ChatGPT repeat is a maximum rating, not a tested result. The only single-pass test I could source is 8 mm, on the Artisan's 40 W module. For the H2D, CNC Kitchen tested only the 10 W laser and published print measurements, not laser ones. The page can tell shoppers to plan on about 8 mm per pass on 40 W and thin stock on 10 W, so the 40 W upgrade (about $700 on the H2D) is worth it only for cutting thick wood.
candidates: Bambu Lab H2D Laser Full Combo (10 W / 40 W)
Bambu Lab H2S Laser Full Combo (10 W)
Snapmaker Artisan (Premium, 40 W laser + 200 W CNC)

findings.label: Single-pass cut thickness, wood (reviewer test)
findings.value: 8 mm wood cut through in one pass
findings.source_title: 3DPrinting.com review: Snapmaker Artisan Premium 3-in-1 Combo (Phillip Keane)
findings.note: Quote: 'cut through 8mm thick wood with a single pass'. The review gives no wood species, speed or power. The page shows no publish date (footer © 2026). The reviewer did not run the CNC because of noise restrictions where they live. This is about half the 15 mm maker rating that the rival pages repeat.

findings.label: Best cut and engrave settings on 5.2 mm basswood (reviewer test)
findings.value: Cut: 1,300 mm/min at 90% power; engrave: 6,000 mm/min at 10% power; the 720 mm/min default was too slow (overheating)
findings.source_title: Review: Can one machine do it all? Snapmaker Artisan Premium 3D printer, CNC, laser (3D Printing Industry, Alex Tyrer-Jones)
findings.note: Published 2025-07-22. In a material test, 1,300 mm/min was the slowest speed that avoided overheating. Pass count is not reported. The reviewer also found air assist 'produced significantly better results' on plywood.

findings.label: Dimensional accuracy (3DPI test, 12 prints per model)
findings.value: Square average deviation 0.134 mm (SD 0.021); hexagon 0.132 mm (SD 0.018); tube 0.064 mm (SD 0.011); a 400 mm tower measured 399.95 mm
findings.source_title: Review: Can one machine do it all? Snapmaker Artisan Premium 3D printer, CNC, laser (3D Printing Industry, Alex Tyrer-Jones)
findings.note: 3DPI's benchmark is an average deviation under 0.1 mm with SD under 0.05 mm, so the square and hexagon miss it and the tube passes. Published 2025-07-22. In dual-extrusion mode the usable print area measured about 400 × 370 mm, not 400 × 400 mm.

findings.label: 3DPI test score
findings.source_title: Review: Can one machine do it all? Snapmaker Artisan Premium 3D printer, CNC, laser (3D Printing Industry, Alex Tyrer-Jones)
findings.note: The same review states both scores, from 3DPI's own test print. Overhangs were clean to 50° with drooping at 60°. This is the only measured figure I found for the Snapmaker 2.0, which ChatGPT showed as its budget pick.

findings.label: Print time, 0.2 mm Benchy (CNC Kitchen)
findings.value: 47 min default profile; 23 min pre-sliced speed Benchy
findings.source_title: I Tested the Bambu Lab H2D (CNC Kitchen, Stefan Hermann)
findings.note: Dated 2025-03-25. Stefan Hermann tested the 10 W laser unit, but the post gives no measured laser cut or engrave figures, only 'up to 5mm thick wood' from the spec.

findings.label: Dual-nozzle two-colour print vs single nozzle (CNC Kitchen)
findings.value: 5 h → 2 h; 129 g → 40 g filament including waste; five-colour octopus 23.5 h → 18.5 h
findings.source_title: I Tested the Bambu Lab H2D (CNC Kitchen, Stefan Hermann)
findings.note: The two-colour figures are for a panda model, comparing the old single-nozzle method with H2D dual-nozzle mode. Hermann says a Prusa XL was 'even five hours less' on the octopus but gives no exact figure.

findings.label: Bed temperature vs setpoint (CNC Kitchen)
findings.source_title: I Tested the Bambu Lab H2D (CNC Kitchen, Stefan Hermann)
findings.note: Measured with a thermal camera and a thermocouple. The article says Bambu Lab later fixed this in firmware. The heated chamber took 'around 10 minutes' to reach 60 °C (the author's estimate).

unsourced: An independent measured laser cut or engrave result for the Bambu Lab H2D or H2S (thickness, passes, speed, time) on either the 10 W or the 40 W module. CNC Kitchen tested the 10 W but published no laser figures. Fauxhammer and 3DBite report none of their own. Overclock3d.net's H2D laser page returned HTTP 403. The Tom's Hardware H2D and H2S reviews returned only the page title to WebFetch, and curl was not approved.

A measured noise level (dB) for any candidate in laser mode from a named reviewer. 3DBite gives only a 'shop-vac' comparison. Snapmaker's own Snapmaker 2.0 enclosure sound test appeared only as a search snippet, and it is the maker's test, so I left it out.
TechRadar's measured results for the Snapmaker 2.0 and the Snapmaker Artisan. Both review pages returned only the title.
The H2D figures from the Independent and from Yahoo Tech ('Don't Buy The Bambu H2D'). The Yahoo page returned HTTP 403, and I did not open the Independent piece.
Today's prices were not checked; they fall outside this angle.
